A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, despite the changed title and substantial reorganization. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renaming.

before.justification: V1 reports original listening studies, objective voice-separation experiments, and instrument/chord probing results in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 reports original tokenizer evaluations, arrangement experiments, listening studies, and retained probing results in Tables 2–6 and 8–9.

M1.justification: The core REMI-z representation, Transformer, reconstruction objective, and instrument/content/history conditioning remain. The source/target selectors clarify existing task-specific operations. Omission of repeated position tokens, newly stated explicitly, is already visible in v1 Figure 2. The new history ablation tests an existing component.

E1.justification: The Los Angeles and Slakh2100 datasets, arrangement coverage, ensemble scenarios, and instrument/chord probes are retained. V1's voice-separation task maps to v2's deterministic band-reconstruction evaluation rather than disappearing. The tokenizer analyses use retained music data; no distinct new domain or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: The piano comparison replaces AccoMontage-3 with the UNet from Terao et al. (2023). The drum comparison replaces Composer's Assistant/T5 with Composer's Assistant 2, identified as v2.1.0 in Appendix B.3. The band comparator's relabeling as Transformer-VAE, with retained subjective scores, is not itself counted as an addition.

E3.justification: V2 replaces most voice-separation metrics with 16th-note Note, instrument-aware Note, and Melody F1, and includes history in the corresponding band-reconstruction evaluation. It adds five-epoch unconditional-LM comparisons and objective piano/drum scoring. Listening feedback groups change from 56/46/45 to 56/73/77. Piano filtering retains about 40% rather than 50%, despite the unchanged pitch-range threshold.

E4.justification: V2 adds tokenizer compactness, entropy, and unconditional-modeling analyses beyond the earlier downstream tokenizer comparison. Table 3 adds a history ablation, while Appendix B.3 reports an octave-shift comparison for UNet. Existing pre-training, voice-conditioning, and instrument/chord probing analyses are retained, with probing moved to Appendix E.

E5.justification: SEM reporting across all three listening studies disappears with v1 Figure 4. Repeated-measures ANOVA remains, with significance marked in v2 Tables 4–6. V2 also removes the explicit statement that experiments were run once, while retaining seed 42; this does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds tokenizer results and substantially revises objective arrangement results. New piano F1 scores are 85.5 for Ours versus 58.3 for UNet; drum scores are 79.3 versus 20.3 for CA v2. Piano/drum listening scores are replaced under changed comparisons and feedback counts, not comparable-setting gains. Band listening scores and both probing tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds entropy and note-normalized perplexity definitions and reasoning in Section 4.2. The metric appendix introduces joint note/instrument matching and replaces melody recall with F1 between highest-average-pitch tracks. These are metric-level mathematical revisions; no new theorem or proof contribution appears.

C1.justification: The central contribution framing shifts from adapting pre-trained models across four named tasks and probing musical knowledge to efficient tokenization as a standalone contribution, three named arrangement tasks, and objective plus perceptual superiority. General tokenizer applicability and pre-training for complex sequence alignment receive substantially greater prominence.

C2.justification: V2 adds entropy/compression and note-perplexity interpretations supporting tokenizer efficiency, and explains disagreement between piano F1 and perceptual quality. Appendix B.3 clarifies accompaniment-only piano reduction and requirements for complete solo reductions; Appendix A discusses velocity omission and performance naturalism. Earlier tempo caveats and probing interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents key normalization, instrument grouping and track merging, baseline reuse/reimplementation, CA v2.1.0, and additional hyperparameters. These disclosures do not establish that previously undocumented preprocessing was newly introduced. V2 supplies a demo address, while code release remains promised upon acceptance.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands tokenizer and pre-trained music-model positioning, adding discussion of works including Pop Music Transformer, Compound Word Transformer, MusicBERT, Multitrack Music Transformer, and MelodyT5. It adds relevant piano/drum literature and organizes prior-method limitations around fragmentation, pre-training compatibility, and arrangement fidelity.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the methods and results are rewritten. V2 introduces numbered sections and organized Appendices A–E, combines objective and subjective findings by arrangement task, and moves probing from the main text into an appendix.

P2.justification: V2 adds the tokenizer comparison figure and efficiency table, promotes the vocabulary table, relocates probing tables, rebuilds the objective arrangement table, and adds F1 columns and significance markers. V1's three-panel error-bar figure is removed, while the reconstruction and tokenization illustrations are retained with revised numbering and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evaluation and reproducibility through objective results, history controls, and preprocessing/baseline documentation. However, it removes SEM reporting and introduces a central entropy inconsistency: REMI-z's reported 29.43 bits/token in Table 2 exceeds the possible Shannon entropy of its fewer-than-1,024-token vocabulary under Equation 2. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a units or computation error. These validity and transparency concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
